info.name: 48Date Backend API
info.description:
The 48Date backend API. Top level splits by **who calls it** (User = the Flutter app, Admin = the Next.js panel); inside each, one folder per module. Kept in sync with every endpoint change — see postman/README.md.

Request bodies hold clean, always-valid JSON (no inline comments — a comment inside a JSON value is invalid data, not documentation); every field is instead documented in the request’s own Description, right below the body. Fields reused across requests in the same flow (phone numbers, OTP codes, tokens, ids) are collection variables, auto-captured by a response script where the value comes from the API, or editable once up top where it’s user input.

request.description:
Watches core services (PostgreSQL database and Redis) for uptime monitors.

**Who can call:** Public (no authentication required).

**Success:** 200 OK when all monitored dependencies are operational.

**Error:** 503 Service Unavailable if any monitored service is down.

**Also available as:** `GET /api/v1/health` (same check, prefixed).

response.name: 200 OK — Healthy
503 Service Unavailable — Dependency Down

request.description:
Watches core services (PostgreSQL database and Redis) directly at root `/health` without the `/api/v1` global prefix (excluded in main.ts). Used by Docker healthchecks, VPS uptime monitors, and load balancers.

**Who can call:** Public (no authentication required).

**Success:** 200 OK when all monitored dependencies are operational.

**Error:** 503 Service Unavailable if any monitored service is down.

response.name: 200 OK — Healthy
503 Service Unavailable — Dependency Down

item.description: Every endpoint the Flutter app calls, one folder per module.

item.name: 01 - Auth
item.description: Module 1 — Phone OTP / Google sign-in, account linking, and session management.

request.description:
Starts phone sign-in: checks Redis rate limits, generates a 6-digit code, stores its hash in Redis (5 min TTL) and enqueues the `sms` job (Twilio delivers it; never sent inline). Public — no auth required. Continue with **02 Verify Phone OTP**.

Rate limits: 60 s cooldown between sends to the same phone, 5/hour and 10/day per phone, 20/hour per IP.

The `{{phone}}` variable is shared with **02 Verify Phone OTP** — change it once here (or in the environment) and both requests stay in sync. `{{devOtp}}` is captured automatically from the response below (only present when DEV_MODE is on and Twilio isn’t configured) for **02 Verify Phone OTP** to use.

**429 countdown:** every rate-limit error (`OTP_COOLDOWN`, `OTP_HOURLY_LIMIT`, `OTP_DAILY_LIMIT`, `OTP_IP_LIMIT`) carries the seconds until the next code can be requested, in two places: `error.details.retryAfterSeconds` (number, in the body) and the standard `Retry-After` header (exposed to browsers via CORS). Use it to show an exact countdown.

**Body fields:**

- `phone` (string, required) — E.164 format — must include the country code, e.g. +8801811000001

response.name: 200 OK — Code sent (DEV_MODE, no Twilio credentials)

request.description:
Verifies the code from **01 Request Phone OTP**, finds or creates the user, issues a session (revoking every other session on this account — single active device policy), and returns the token pair. A `BANNED` account is rejected; a `DELETED` account within its 90-day window is restored automatically (`restored: true`). Public — no auth required.

Uses `{{phone}}` and `{{devOtp}}` captured by **01 Request Phone OTP** — run that first. On success, `{{accessToken}}`/`{{refreshToken}}` are captured here for every bearer-auth request below.

**Body fields:**

- `phone` (string, required) — E.164 format, must match the phone used in 01 Request Phone OTP
- `otp` (string, required) — 6-digit code — auto-filled from 01 Request Phone OTP in DEV_MODE; replace with the real SMS code otherwise
- `device` (object, optional) — recorded on the user session:
 - `device.platform` (string, optional) — client platform (case-sensitive, one of: `"android"`, `"ios"`, `"web"`)
 - `device.appVersion` (string, optional) — semver app version string (e.g. `"1.4.0"`)
 - `device.deviceName` (string, optional) — human-readable device model (e.g. `"Pixel 8"`, `"iPhone 15 Pro"`)

request.description:
Verifies the Google ID token (signature, issuer, audience against `GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS`), finds or creates the user by `googleSub`, issues a session (one device at a time). Public — no auth required.

**Body fields:**

- `idToken` (string, required) — from the Google Sign-In SDK on the client; cannot be auto-filled
- `device` (object, optional) — recorded on the user session:
 - `device.platform` (string, optional) — client platform (case-sensitive, one of: `"android"`, `"ios"`, `"web"`)
 - `device.appVersion` (string, optional) — semver app version string (e.g. `"1.4.0"`)
 - `device.deviceName` (string, optional) — human-readable device model (e.g. `"Pixel 8"`, `"iPhone 15 Pro"`)

request.description:
Rotates the refresh token: the presented token is invalidated and a new access/refresh pair is issued for the same session (the session id does not change). Presenting a token that was already rotated or revoked is treated as token theft — the whole session family is revoked and the account must sign in again.

**Grace window (D-231):** for a short time after a rotation (`auth.refresh.graceSeconds`, default **60 s**, super admin can set 0–300 in Platform Settings → Security; 0 = off), sending the **old** token again returns `200` with the **same** new pair the rotation issued — no sign-out. This covers a refresh response lost to a page reload, closed tab or dropped network, and two refresh calls racing each other. If the new token was itself rotated again since, the latest pair is returned. After the window, or after logout / a new sign-in, the old token gets `401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED` as before.

**Client rules:** run only one refresh at a time (other requests wait for it; across browser tabs use the Web Locks API or a `BroadcastChannel`); save the new `accessToken` + `refreshToken` immediately, before retrying anything; on `401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED` or `REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID`, clear the stored tokens and go to sign-in — never retry. Public endpoint (the refresh token itself is the credential) — no bearer header needed.

Uses and replaces `{{refreshToken}}`.

**Body fields:**

- `refreshToken` (string, required) — from 02 Verify Phone OTP, 03 Google Sign-In, or a previous call to this endpoint

response.name: 200 OK — Rotated successfully

**Client rules:** run only one refresh at a time (other requests wait for it; across browser tabs use the Web Locks API or a `BroadcastChannel`); save the new `accessToken` + `refreshToken` immediately, before retrying anything; on `401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED` or `REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID`, clear the stored tokens and go to sign-in — never retry. Public endpoint (the refresh token itself is the credential) — no bearer header needed.

Uses and replaces `{{refreshToken}}`.

**Body fields:**

- `refreshToken` (string, required) — from 02 Verify Phone OTP, 03 Google Sign-In, or a previous call to this endpoint

request.description:
Same OTP engine as sign-in, purpose `LINK`, with standard rate limits. Checked up front that the phone is not already linked to another account. **Auth:** bearer access token required.

`{{linkPhone}}` is a separate variable from `{{phone}}` (the sign-in number) so you can link a second number without overwriting it. `{{linkDevOtp}}` is captured automatically for **10 Link Phone — Verify OTP**.

**429 countdown:** every rate-limit error (`OTP_COOLDOWN`, `OTP_HOURLY_LIMIT`, `OTP_DAILY_LIMIT`, `OTP_IP_LIMIT`) carries the seconds until the next code can be requested, in two places: `error.details.retryAfterSeconds` (number, in the body) and the standard `Retry-After` header (exposed to browsers via CORS). Use it to show an exact countdown.

**Body fields:**

- `phone` (string, required) — E.164 format, the number to link — different from the sign-in phone

**Errors:** `409 PHONE_ALREADY_SET` when the account already has a phone number (linking never replaces a phone; a "change phone" flow comes later). `409 PHONE_ALREADY_LINKED` when the number belongs to another account. Checked before any SMS is sent.

item.description: Module 2: Users (Onboarding, Profile, Central Uploads, Face Verification, and Self-Deletion).

request.description:
Retrieves current onboarding state for the signed-in user: overall status (`NOT_STARTED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED`), next pending step key, progress percentage, step states (`PENDING`, `DONE`, `SKIPPED`), and previously saved values.

**`savedValues` shape convention:**
- Only steps whose state is `DONE` are included (placeholder defaults for uncompleted steps are omitted).
- Single-value scalar steps (`nickname`, `smoking`, `drinking`, `gender`, `interested_in`, `height`, `weight`, `looking_for`, `education`, `religion`, `bio`) return a primitive (`string` or `number`).
- Multi-value steps (`languages`, `interests`, `photos`) return an array. When `photos` is `DONE`, returns at most `photos.galleryMaxLimit` photos (default: 50, capped via Prisma `take` in query, main photo first), alongside `photoCount` indicating the user's total photo count.
- Multi-field steps (`location`, `real_name`, `birthday`, `kids`) return an object (`real_name` is `{ "saved": true }`; public real names are strictly excluded per D-118).

request.description:
Initiates face verification with uploaded V-pose selfie. Returns HTTP 202 Accepted with snapshot.

**Body fields:**
- `selfieFileId` (string, required): UUID of uploaded file with purpose VERIFICATION_SELFIE
- `accessibilityRequested` (boolean, optional): Set true if user has hand differences or motor limitations preventing the V-pose gesture; routes to admin review without auto-reject penalty (DF-03, D-211)

**Prerequisites:** User must have uploaded profile photos (at least one main photo) beforehand; otherwise returns 400 `PROFILE_PHOTO_REQUIRED`.

**Notifications sent:** When the background check passes, the user receives `VERIFICATION_PASSED`. If rejected, `VERIFICATION_REJECTED`.

**One attempt at a time (B2):** while another selfie is still being checked → `409 VERIFICATION_IN_PROGRESS`. Starting here expires any open verification link (its SSE emits `expired`). The attempt is recorded with `source: APP` (link submissions use `WEB_LINK`).

**Camera not working?** Offer `29 Create Verification Link` (verify on another device).

**No internal user ids (D-239, 2026-11-21):** the snapshot no longer has `userId` (it is always you). The person is always identified by nickname.

request.description:
**Verify on another device (B2).** For devices whose camera doesn't work: creates a one-time link the user opens in **any browser on any device — the same phone or a different one** — to take and submit the selfie. Offered on both verification screens (onboarding and profile).

**Rules:**
- The link is valid for `verification.linkLifetimeMinutes` (admin setting, default **15 min**) and works **once**.
- Creating a link **expires any open link** (its SSE emits `expired`, the old URL stops working). Starting verification in the app does the same.
- While a submitted selfie is still being checked, new links are rejected (`409 VERIFICATION_IN_PROGRESS`).
- Needs a profile photo first (D-212, `400 PROFILE_PHOTO_REQUIRED`).
- Max `verification.linkMaxPerDay` links per user per 24 h (default 10, `429 VERIFICATION_LINK_LIMIT_REACHED`). The selfie itself also counts toward the normal daily attempt limit (D-210).
- Admins can switch the feature off (`verification.linkEnabled`, `503 VERIFICATION_LINK_DISABLED`).

**Response `data`:** the link snapshot plus `token` (string — shown only here), `url` (`{verification.linkBaseUrl}/{token}` — put it in a QR code / Copy / Open button; `null` if no base URL is configured) and `eventsUrl` (SSE to follow the result).

**Link states (case-sensitive):** `WAITING` (created, not opened) → `OPENED` (the browser page loaded the token) → `SUBMITTED` (selfie sent; `verificationId` + `verificationStatus` now set) → `PASSED` / `NEEDS_REVIEW` (admin queue) / `FAILED`; or `EXPIRED` (lifetime passed, or revoked by a new link / an in-app attempt). After `SUBMITTED` the status follows the verification itself, so a later admin approval shows as `PASSED`.

**App flow:** show the QR/link → open `eventsUrl` (or poll `30 Get Verification Link`) → on `passed` go to the next onboarding step / show the verified badge. Backups: `VERIFICATION_PASSED` / `VERIFICATION_REJECTED` push, `28 Get My Verification Status`.

**Body fields:** none.

**Notifications sent:** none (the result push comes later from the verification itself).

**Who can call:** Authenticated user (also during onboarding).

**Variables:** reads `{{accessToken}}`; sets `verificationLinkId`, `verificationLinkToken`.

**Who can call:** Authenticated user (the link owner).

request.description:
Updates profile fields after onboarding. Nickname and real name cannot be changed.

**Body fields:**
All fields are optional; send only what changes. A field you leave out keeps its saved value.
- `occupation` (string, optional, max 50).
- `smoking` (string, optional, case-sensitive): `REGULARLY`, `OCCASIONALLY`, `NEVER`.
- `drinking` (string, optional, case-sensitive): `REGULARLY`, `SOCIALLY`, `NEVER`.
- `gender` (string, optional, case-sensitive): `WOMAN`, `MAN`, `PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY` (legacy values `MALE`, `FEMALE`, `OTHER` are still accepted; don't use them).
- `hasKids` (boolean, optional).
- `wantsKids` (boolean, optional).
- `interestedIn` (string, optional, case-sensitive): `WOMEN`, `MEN`, `EVERYONE`.
- `heightCm` (integer, optional): 120–230.
- `weightKg` (integer, optional): 30–250.
- `lookingFor` (string, optional, case-sensitive): `REAL_RELATIONSHIP`, `SOMETHING_MEANINGFUL`, `SEE_WHERE_IT_GOES`, `NEW_FRIENDS_FIRST`.
- `languageCodes` (string[], optional): ISO 639-1 codes, e.g. `["bn","en"]`.
- `educationLevel` (string, optional, case-sensitive): `HIGH_SCHOOL`, `DIPLOMA`, `BACHELORS`, `MASTERS`, `DOCTORATE`, `OTHER`.
- `religion` (string, optional, case-sensitive): `ISLAM`, `HINDUISM`, `CHRISTIANITY`, `BUDDHISM`, `SIKHISM`, `JUDAISM`, `OTHER`, `NOT_RELIGIOUS`.
- `bio` (string, optional, max 300).
- `interestIds` (UUID[], optional): ids from `GET /onboarding/options` interests; replaces the whole list.
- `hideOnlineStatus` (boolean, optional): `true` needs the `HIDE_ONLINE_STATUS` entitlement, otherwise `403 ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED`.

- `nickname` (string, optional, **locked**): only the current value is accepted; a different one → `400` "Nickname cannot be changed once chosen (D-117)". Don't send it.
- `firstName` (string, optional, **locked**): any value → `400` "Real name is locked after onboarding…". Don't send it.
- `lastName` (string, optional, **locked**): same as `firstName`.
- `birthDate` (string, optional, **locked**): any value → `400` "Birth date is locked after onboarding…". Don't send it.

**Route Aliases:**
- Primary: `PATCH /api/v1/users/me/profile`
- Alias: `PATCH /api/v1/users/me` (both routes map to the same profile update handler).

**Also available as:** `PATCH /users/me` (same handler).

request.description:
Refreshes the caller's location (D-54). Location is required for discovery.

**Who can call:** authenticated user (Bearer token).

**Two valid calls:**
- **New fix:** `latitude` + `longitude` together (plus `city` only when you have a reverse-geocoded name, plus `permission`).
- **Permission change only:** `permission` alone (e.g. the user denied location).

**`city` rule (important):** every field is optional, and a field you **leave out keeps its saved value**. On a coordinates-only refresh, **leave `city` out**; don't send `null` or `""`. Sending `"city": null` **erases** the saved city, and discovery cards then show no area.

**Response:** the **stored** location after the update (fields you left out show their kept values), not an echo of the request.

**Body fields:**
- `latitude` (number, optional): WGS-84 decimal degrees, -90 to 90. Required together with `longitude`.
- `longitude` (number, optional): WGS-84 decimal degrees, -180 to 180. Required together with `latitude`.

item.name: 03 Start or Resume Discovery Deck Run

request.description:
Starts or resumes a discovery deck build.

**Who can call:** Authenticated user (Bearer token).

**Behavior (in order):**
1. A run `QUEUED` or `RUNNING` → `200`, `reused: true`.
2. **Double tap:** a run created in the last few seconds (admin setting `deckRuns.duplicateTapWindowSeconds`, default 5) → `200`, `reused: true` — even with `refresh: true`.
3. A fresh `COMPLETED` deck (younger than `deckRuns.deckFreshnessHours`, default 24 h) that still has cards **or found no one at all** (`deckSize: 0`) → `200`, `reused: true`. An empty deck is reused on purpose: show **"No new profiles right now"** instead of starting a new run on every visit. A deck the user already swiped through is rebuilt.
4. Otherwise a new run is created (`QUEUED`), a background job is enqueued → `202`, `reused: false`.

**Hourly limit (admin-tunable):** at most `deckRuns.maxRunsPerHour` (default 20) new runs per user per hour; only runs still in progress or that found cards count — failed and empty runs don't. Admins can switch it off (`deckRuns.rateLimitEnabled`). Over the limit → `429 DISCOVERY_RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (seconds) and `error.details.retryAfterSeconds` + `error.details.limit`; `message` is ready to show the user (includes the wait).

**App guidance:** call this once per visit to Discover, not on every render.

**Body fields:**
- `refresh` (boolean, optional): `true` skips reusing a fresh deck and builds a new one (double-tap rule and hourly limit still apply). Default `false`.

**Side effects:** enqueues a job on the `discovery` BullMQ queue.

**Variables:** reads `{{accessToken}}`; sets `discoveryRunId` on success.

response.name: 202 Queued New Deck Run
200 Reused Active/Fresh Run
403 Onboarding Incomplete
409 Location Required
429 Too Many Requests — Discover Refreshed Too Often

request.description:
Real-time Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream for discovery deck builds.

**Who can call:** Authenticated user.
**Stream Lifecycle:**
1. Emits initial `snapshot` event immediately upon connection.
2. Emits `progress` events as worker completes pipeline stages (`VIEWER_CONTEXT`, `CANDIDATES`, `ELIGIBILITY`, `ORDER`, `STORE_DECK`).
3. Emits terminal `completed` or `failed` event, then server closes connection.
4. Sends `: ping` comments every 15 seconds to keep connection alive.

**Unknown or someone else's id:** a normal JSON error before any stream data (`404`; a verification that belongs to another user gives `403`). The stream itself only opens for a valid id. A failed run ends with `event: failed` and `data: { id, status: "FAILED", stage: "FAILED", progressPercent: 100, error: { code } }`. A `ping` event is sent every 15 s.

request.description:
Records a user swipe (`PASS` or `LIKE`) synchronously.

**Who can call:** Authenticated user.
**Rules:**
- `targetNickname` is resolved to internal user ID.
- Cannot swipe on oneself (`400 SWIPE_SELF`).
- Cannot swipe on unavailable or blocked user (`409 USER_UNAVAILABLE`).
- Repeating the same action is idempotent.
- `PASS` -> `LIKE` is allowed (recycled profile after 30 days).
- `LIKE` -> `PASS` is forbidden (`409 SWIPE_ALREADY_DECIDED`). A like is permanent.
- When a `LIKE` is mutual, creates a match in Module 4 inside the same transaction and returns popup details.

**Body fields:**
- `targetNickname`: string (required) — Permanent nickname of candidate.
- `action` (string, required, case-sensitive): `PASS`, `LIKE`, `SUPER_LIKE` (`SUPER_LIKE` uses the weekly super-like allowance; when it is used up → `429 SUPER_LIKES_EXHAUSTED`).
- `source`: string (optional, case-sensitive) — `DECK` | `PROFILE`. Default `DECK`.
- `runId`: string (optional) — Discovery run UUID if swiped from deck.

**Side effects:** Emits `discovery.swiped` and `discovery.liked` counters; on mutual match, queues `MATCH_NEW` push notification.

**Super Like (DF-05, D-204):**
- Passing `action: 'SUPER_LIKE'` consumes from the user's weekly allowance.
- Sends immediate push notification `SUPER_LIKE_RECEIVED` to recipient.
- Places the sender at the front of the recipient's card deck stack with `isSuperLike: true`.
- If recipient already swiped LIKE or SUPER_LIKE, creates an instant Match popup.

request.description:
Undoes the single most recent swipe (DF-07, D-204, D-205).

**Mechanics:**
- Reads `discovery:last_swipe:{userId}` from Redis.
- Fails with 404 `NO_SWIPE_TO_UNDO` if no recent swipe exists.
- Fails with 410 `UNDO_TIME_EXPIRED` if the time window (`rewindTimeLimitMinutes`, default 15 mins) has elapsed.
- Fails with 409 `CANNOT_UNDO_MATCHED_SWIPE` if the swipe already formed an active match (D-204 safe boundary).
- In MVP: All users can undo (paywalls hidden per D-189/D-190/D-197; `rewindAllowedForFree: true`).
- Post-MVP: Rejects with 403 `REWIND_PREMIUM_ONLY` if admin sets `rewindAllowedForFree: false` and user lacks `UNDO_SWIPE` entitlement.
- Deletes the `Swipe` record from PostgreSQL.
- Re-inserts the candidate card onto the front of the user's active Redis deck (`discovery:deck:{runId}`).
- Clears `discovery:last_swipe:{userId}` (1-step undo only, D-204).
- Returns the restored candidate card representation.

**Route Aliases:**
- Primary: `POST /api/v1/discovery/deck/undo`
- Alias: `POST /api/v1/discovery/swipes/undo` (both routes invoke the single-step swipe rewind).

**Also available as:** `POST /discovery/swipes/undo` (same handler, same response).

request.description:
Connects to the real-time Socket.IO chat gateway.

### 1. Connection & Handshake
- **Protocol:** Socket.IO v4
- **HTTP Handshake URL:** `{{socketUrl}}/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling&token={{accessToken}}`
- **WebSocket URL (Flutter App):** `ws://localhost:3000/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=websocket&token={{accessToken}}`
- **Authentication:** Pass the Bearer access token either via handshake header:
 `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}`
 or query parameter:
 `?token={{accessToken}}`

### 2. Client → Server Events
| Event | Payload | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `joinConversation` | `{"conversationId": "uuid"}` | Join conversation room (`conversation:{id}`). |
| `leaveConversation` | `{"conversationId": "uuid"}` | Leave conversation room. |
| `typing` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "isTyping": true}` | Relay typing indicator to room (relayed only, never stored in DB). |
| `message:delivered` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "upToSeq": 42}` | Advance `deliveredUpToSeq` pointer in `conversation_members`. |
| `message:seen` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "upToSeq": 42}` | Advance `seenUpToSeq` pointer in `conversation_members`. |
| `heartbeat` | `{}` | Refreshes Redis online presence TTL (60s). |

### 3. Server → Client Events
| Event | Payload | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `message:new` | `MessageItemDto` | Full new message (delivered to room and recipient's user room). |
| `conversation:receipt` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "nickname": "str", "deliveredUpToSeq": int, "seenUpToSeq": int}` | Partner's delivery or seen pointer moved. |
| `typing` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "nickname": "str", "isTyping": bool}` | Partner typing status update. |
| `presence` | `{"nickname": "str", "online": bool, "lastSeenAt": "iso"}` | Partner presence status. |
| `conversation:closed` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "reason": "EXPIRED \| BLOCKED"}` | Conversation closed upon match expiry or block.

**Query parameters:**
- `EIO` (string, required): Engine.IO protocol version (`4`).
- `transport` (string, required): Transport mechanism (`polling` for HTTP handshake, `websocket` for Flutter socket).
- `token` (string, optional): Bearer access token for handshake authentication.
| `message:edited` | `{"messageId": "uuid", "conversationId": "uuid", "text": "str", "isEdited": true, "editedAt": "iso"}` | Broadcast when a message is edited. |
| `message:deleted` | `{"messageId": "uuid", "conversationId": "uuid", "isDeleted": true, "deletedAt": "iso"}` | Broadcast when a message is soft-deleted. |

**No internal user ids (D-239, 2026-11-21):** messages no longer carry `senderId`; use `senderNickname` and `isMine`. Date bubble `payload` no longer carries `proposerId` / `receiverId` (older bubbles have them removed too); the proposer is the bubble's sender (`isMine` / `senderNickname`). The person is always identified by nickname.

originalRequest.description:
Connects to the real-time Socket.IO chat gateway.

### 1. Connection & Handshake
- **Protocol:** Socket.IO v4
- **HTTP Handshake URL:** `{{socketUrl}}/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling&token={{accessToken}}`
- **WebSocket URL (Flutter App):** `ws://localhost:3000/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=websocket&token={{accessToken}}`
- **Authentication:** Pass the Bearer access token either via handshake header:
 `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}`
 or query parameter:
 `?token={{accessToken}}`

### 2. Client → Server Events
| Event | Payload | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `joinConversation` | `{"conversationId": "uuid"}` | Join conversation room (`conversation:{id}`). |
| `leaveConversation` | `{"conversationId": "uuid"}` | Leave conversation room. |
| `typing` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "isTyping": true}` | Relay typing indicator to room (relayed only, never stored in DB). |
| `message:delivered` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "upToSeq": 42}` | Advance `deliveredUpToSeq` pointer in `conversation_members`. |
| `message:seen` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "upToSeq": 42}` | Advance `seenUpToSeq` pointer in `conversation_members`. |
| `heartbeat` | `{}` | Refreshes Redis online presence TTL (60s). |

### 3. Server → Client Events
| Event | Payload | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `message:new` | `MessageItemDto` | Full new message (delivered to room and recipient's user room). |
| `conversation:receipt` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "nickname": "str", "deliveredUpToSeq": int, "seenUpToSeq": int}` | Partner's delivery or seen pointer moved. |
| `typing` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "nickname": "str", "isTyping": bool}` | Partner typing status update. |
| `presence` | `{"nickname": "str", "online": bool, "lastSeenAt": "iso"}` | Partner presence status. |
| `conversation:closed` | `{"conversationId": "uuid", "reason": "EXPIRED \| BLOCKED"}` | Conversation closed upon match expiry or block.

**Query parameters:**
- `EIO` (string, required): Engine.IO protocol version (`4`).
- `transport` (string, required): Transport mechanism (`polling` for HTTP handshake, `websocket` for Flutter socket).
- `token` (string, optional): Bearer access token for handshake authentication.
| `message:edited` | `{"messageId": "uuid", "conversationId": "uuid", "text": "str", "isEdited": true, "editedAt": "iso"}` | Broadcast when a message is edited. |
| `message:deleted` | `{"messageId": "uuid", "conversationId": "uuid", "isDeleted": true, "deletedAt": "iso"}` | Broadcast when a message is soft-deleted. |

**No internal user ids (D-239, 2026-11-21):** messages no longer carry `senderId`; use `senderNickname` and `isMine`. Date bubble `payload` no longer carries `proposerId` / `receiverId` (older bubbles have them removed too); the proposer is the bubble's sender (`isMine` / `senderNickname`). The person is always identified by nickname.

request.description:
Retrieves cursor-paginated list of active conversations for the authenticated user.

Each conversation includes the partner's UserSummary, last message preview, unread count, and the 48-hour countdown timer pill (active while clock runs, hidden once a date plan is accepted and the match is safe).

**Query parameters:**
- `cursor` (string, optional): ISO date string of oldest item from previous page.
- `limit` (integer, optional): Items per page, default 20, max 50.

**Blocked users (D-226):** conversations with a user either side has blocked are never listed. They are filtered in the query, so every page is full and `meta.hasMore` is exact.

request.description:
Starts a new game or retrieves the active/completed game for this conversation (strictly one game per conversation).

When a new game starts, the AI analyzes both participants' profiles (shared & distinct interests, hobbies, occupation, lifestyle) and generates 10 tailored, personalized 'This or That' dilemma questions (DF-11, D-208) with `isAiGenerated: true` and `category` tags. If AI generation is disabled or fails, the engine seamlessly falls back to 10 active admin-managed questions with `isAiGenerated: false`.

An immutable snapshot of the 10 questions is stored on the game record and an invitation bubble is posted into the chat conversation.

**Path parameters:**
- `conversationId` (UUID, required): Conversation ID owning the game.

**Body fields:**
- `gameType` (string, optional, default: `"THIS_OR_THAT"`): Allowed value: `THIS_OR_THAT` (case-sensitive).
- `conversationId` (string, optional): Also supported directly on `POST /games` payload.

**Notifications sent:** When a new game is created, the partner receives `GAME_INVITE` (push + in-app inbox, target screen `GAME`, `targetParams: { gameId, conversationId }`). Returning an existing game sends nothing.

**Route Aliases:**
- Primary: `POST /api/v1/conversations/:id/games` (with `:id` in the path)
- Alias: `POST /api/v1/games` with JSON body `{ "conversationId": "{{conversationId}}" }`.

**Also available as:** `POST /games` with `conversationId` in the body (same handler; `400 BAD_REQUEST` "conversationId is required" when it is missing).

request.description:
Retrieves game questions, personal answers, and revealed partner answers.

**No Peeking Rule:**
The server strictly hides the partner's choice for question $N$ until the requesting user has answered question $N$ themselves (`partnerChoice: null`, `partnerAnswered: true/false`). Once answered, both choices and match status (`isMatch`) are immediately revealed.

**Path parameters:**
- `gameId` (UUID, required): Game ID.

response.name: 200 OK — Game State with No-Peeking Masking
200 OK — Game Completed (Result Revealed)

request.description:
Submits an answer (`A` or `B`) for a question in an in-progress game.

**Sequential Progression Rule:**
Questions must be answered strictly in order (Question 1 of 10 through Question 10 of 10). Skipping questions or attempting later questions out of sequence returns `400 Bad Request` (`GAME_QUESTION_OUT_OF_ORDER`).

If the partner has already answered this question, the match result is revealed immediately (`isMatch: true/false`). When both players complete all 10 questions, the game status transitions to `COMPLETED`, a result bubble is posted in the chat, and `game:completed` is broadcast over Socket.IO.

**Path parameters:**
- `gameId` (UUID, required): Game ID.

**Body fields:**
- `questionId` (UUID, required): The question ID in the game snapshot.
- `choice` (enum, required): Selected option: `A` or `B` (case-sensitive).

**Notifications sent:** When the last answer completes the game, both players receive `GAME_COMPLETED` (push + in-app inbox, target screen `GAME`).

**Closed conversations:** a block closes the conversation and every game still `IN_PROGRESS` in it (D-226); answering then returns `409 CONVERSATION_CLOSED` (or `409 GAME_CLOSED` once the game itself is closed).

request.description:
Initiates or returns cached venue suggestions around the fuzzed midpoint between both matched users.

Midpoint is fuzzed by ~1 km to safeguard user privacy. Returns curated venues with one highlighted as the AI Pick (Claude Haiku 4.5).

**`distanceKmFromMe`:** always measured from **you** (the signed-in caller) to the venue, in km with one decimal. Both people in the match get their own distance.

Progressive Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream for venue suggestions and AI recommendation pick.

**Who can call:** Authenticated match participants.

**Pre-stream validation:** Validates run existence (`404 RUN_NOT_FOUND`) and match membership (`403 NOT_MATCH_PARTICIPANT`) as JSON before opening the SSE stream.

**Events emitted:** `queued`, `venues`, `completed`.

**Event format:** the stream sends unnamed SSE messages (no `event:` line); the event type is inside the JSON as `data.event` (`queued`, `venues`, `completed`, `failed`). Venue items have the same fields as `02 Get Venue Suggestions`.

**`distanceKmFromMe`:** always measured from **you** (the signed-in caller) to the venue, in km with one decimal. Both people in the match get their own distance. This also applies to the live `venues` and `completed` events (fixed 2026-11-21: they used to carry the other person's distance for one of the two users).

**Path parameters:**
- `id` (UUID, required): The date plan identifier.

**Viewer-relative fields (D-228):** internal user ids never leave the server. Date plans carry `proposedByMe` (boolean: you sent the invitation) instead of `proposerId` / `receiverId`, and `cancelledByMe` (boolean once cancelled, `null` when not cancelled or cancelled by a block) instead of `cancelledBy`. The person is always `counterpart` (by nickname).

**Blocks (D-228):** while either user blocks the other, their dates are hidden: they are left out of `GET /dates` and `GET /dates/{id}` / `GET /dates/{id}/history` return `404 DATE_NOT_FOUND`. After an unblock they show again, still `CANCELLED` with `cancelReason: "UNAVAILABLE"`.

request.description:
Confirms attendance for a date once its scheduled calendar time has passed (Mobile screens `M / ATTENDANCE` and `M / ATTENDANCE-WAIT`).

### Two-Sided Attendance Confirmation (D-203)
When a date passes its scheduled time, it transitions from `SET` to `AWAITING_CONFIRMATION`:
1. **Screen 1 (`ATTENDANCE` — "Did you meet {partner}?"):**
   - User chooses: "Yes, we met" (`attended = true`) or "No, we didn't meet" (`attended = false`).
2. **Screen 2 (`ATTENDANCE-WAIT` — "Your confirmation is saved"):**
   - Displays "We're waiting for {partner}'s response." with status badge "• Awaiting both responses".
   - Provides action buttons "Leave feedback" (proceeds to date ratings) and "Back to matches".

### State Transitions
- **If partner has not confirmed yet:** The date stays in status `AWAITING_CONFIRMATION`. The response returns `bothConfirmed: false` and `completed: false`. Partner receives a notification asking them to confirm.
- **If both participants confirm `attended = true`:** The date immediately transitions to `COMPLETED` (`completedAt` is recorded). Socket event `date:completed` is broadcast, the chat date bubble updates to `COMPLETED`, and both participants are notified to leave feedback / rate each other.
- **If either participant confirms `attended = false`:** The date transitions to `NO_SHOW` (and appropriate trust score event is logged).

**Who can call:** Authenticated participant (`proposer` or `receiver`) of the date plan.
**Side effects:** Saves participant's attendance confirmation; transitions date to `COMPLETED` or `NO_SHOW` when both have responded; emits WebSocket events `date:confirmed` or `date:completed`.

**Body fields:**
- `attended` (boolean, required) — `true` ("Yes, we met") or `false` ("No, we didn't meet").
- `note` (string, optional, max 500 characters) — optional attendance comment.

*Note on pagination:* This endpoint returns the bounded change history of a single date plan. It is unpaginated by design.

**Path parameters:**
- `id` (UUID, required): The date plan identifier.

**`cancelReason` values:** `DECLINED`, `WITHDRAWN`, `UNAVAILABLE` (the date was cancelled automatically because the match became unavailable — a block, D-226/D-228; no trust penalty, no notification, `cancelledByMe` is `null`; show a neutral "This date was cancelled", never say who or why), or the free-text reason the canceller chose.

**Viewer-relative fields (D-228):** internal user ids never leave the server. Date plans carry `proposedByMe` (boolean: you sent the invitation) instead of `proposerId` / `receiverId`, and `cancelledByMe` (boolean once cancelled, `null` when not cancelled or cancelled by a block) instead of `cancelledBy`. Postpone/cancel requests carry `requestedByMe` (boolean) and `respondedByMe` (boolean once answered, `null` while pending) instead of `requestedBy` / `respondedBy`. The person is always `counterpart` (by nickname).

**Blocks (D-228):** while either user blocks the other, their dates are hidden: they are left out of `GET /dates` and `GET /dates/{id}` / `GET /dates/{id}/history` return `404 DATE_NOT_FOUND`. After an unblock they show again, still `CANCELLED` with `cancelReason: "UNAVAILABLE"`.

request.description:
Requests 3 AI-generated reply suggestions upon tapping ✨ in the chat.

### Core Rules:
- **Instant Reuse:** If no new message arrived in this conversation since the last request, returns the cached suggestions instantly (`isCached: true`) without consuming a daily tap.
- **Date Nudge:** While the 48-hour clock is running, at least one suggestion casually nudges toward planning a date.
- **Tone Selection:** Gated by the `AI_TONE_SELECT` plan entitlement.

**Path parameters:**
- `conversationId` (UUID, required): The target conversation identifier.

**Body fields:**
- `tone` (string, optional): Desired suggestion tone. Allowed values (case-sensitive): `FLIRTY`, `CASUAL`, `WITTY`.

**Response capture:**
Saves `data.requestId` into collection variable `{{aiRequestId}}`.

request.description:
Submits a safety/moderation report against another member. Severity is assigned by the server. If a pending report already exists between these users, new details are merged. Does NOT penalize target score until an admin reviews and acts.

**Body fields:**
- `reportedNickname` (string, required*): nickname of the user being reported. *One of `reportedNickname`, `targetNickname` or `reportedUserId` must be sent (`targetNickname` / `reportedUserId` are legacy aliases; each accepts a nickname); none → `400`.
- `reason` (string, optional, max 100): reason key from `GET /reports/reasons` (e.g. `FAKE_PROFILE`). Default `OTHER`. Legacy alias: `category`.
- `subReason` (string, optional, max 100): sub-reason key from the same list.
- `description` (string, optional, max 500): free-text details.
- `source` (string, optional, case-sensitive): `PROFILE`, `CHAT`, `DATE`.
- `conversationId` (string, optional): the chat the report came from (source `CHAT`).
- `datePlanId` (string, optional): the date the report is about (source `DATE`). Legacy alias: `dateId`.
- `alsoBlock` (boolean, optional): also block the user in the same call. Legacy alias: `blockUser`.
Severity is set by the server from the reason (D-152); the app never sends it.
- `targetNickname` (string, optional): legacy alias of `reportedNickname`. Use `reportedNickname`.
- `reportedUserId` (string, optional): legacy alias of `reportedNickname` (accepts a nickname). Use `reportedNickname`.
- `category` (string, optional): legacy alias of `reason`. Use `reason`.
- `dateId` (string, optional): legacy alias of `datePlanId`. Use `datePlanId`.
- `blockUser` (boolean, optional): legacy alias of `alsoBlock`. Use `alsoBlock`.

**Who can call:** Authenticated user.

**No internal user ids (D-239, 2026-11-21):** `reporterId` / `reportedUserId` were removed; use `reportedNickname`. The person is always identified by nickname.

Blocks another member by **nickname**. The block works both ways.

**What a block does (D-102, D-226), in one transaction:**
- Records the block (re-blocking a previously unblocked user re-activates the old record).
- Sets their match to `UNMATCHED` (it disappears from both users' matches; `GET /matches/{id}` returns `404 MATCH_NOT_FOUND`).
- Closes their conversation (`closedReason: BLOCKED`) and any game still `IN_PROGRESS` in it (`CLOSED`).
- Cancels every open date of the match (`REQUESTED` / `SET`) (stored as `BLOCKED`; both users see `cancelReason: "UNAVAILABLE"` with `cancelledByMe: null`, and the dates are hidden from both while the block lasts, D-228), expires pending postpone requests. **No trust penalty** for either user.
- Sends Socket.IO `conversation:closed` `{ conversationId, reason: "BLOCKED" }` once to both users and removes their sockets from the conversation room (see WebSockets collection → `06 conversation:closed — User Blocked`).
- Hides each user from the other everywhere: discovery, likes received, chats list, notifications.

**Notifications sent:** none (no push, no inbox item, no `date:cancelled` event — the blocked user is not told).

**Body fields:**
- `nickname` (string, required): public nickname of the target user, matched case-insensitively. Sending `userId` (or any other field) is rejected with `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` — internal ids never leave or enter the API (D-120, D-123).
- `source` (enum, optional): where the block started. Case-sensitive allowed values: `CHAT`, `PROFILE`, `REPORT`. Default `CHAT`.

**Response `data`:** `{ message, blockedNickname }`.

**Who can call:** Authenticated user.

**Variables:** reads `{{accessToken}}`, `{{targetNickname}}`.

request.description:
Unblocks a user I blocked. The block record keeps its history (`unblockedAt`).

**What comes back (D-227, supersedes D-154)** — only once **no block remains either way** (if both blocked each other, both must unblock), and only what the block closed:
- The match → `ACTIVE` again, back in both matches lists. A **safe** match (a date was accepted) stays timer-free; otherwise it gets a **fresh 48 h** clock.
- The conversation → `OPEN` again with its full history, back in both chats lists.
- A game the block closed → `IN_PROGRESS` again with its answers.
- **Not restored:** dates the block cancelled stay `CANCELLED` (`cancelReason: "BLOCKED"`) — send a new invite. A match that had expired before the block, or that an admin ended, stays as it is.
- Discovery, profile view and notifications between the two resume.

**Socket:** both users get `conversation:reopened` `{ conversationId }` (WebSockets collection → `21 conversation:reopened — Chat Restored After Unblock`).

**Notifications sent:** none (no push, no inbox item, no system message in the chat).

**Path variables:**
- `nickname` (string, required): public nickname of the target user, matched case-insensitively.

**Response `data`:** `message` (string), `unblockedNickname` (string), `restored` (boolean — `true` when the match, chat and game came back; `false` when nothing was restored, e.g. the other user still blocks you, or there was no match).

**Who can call:** Authenticated user.

**Variables:** reads `{{accessToken}}`, `{{targetNickname}}`.

request.description:
Retrieves the authenticated user's cursor-paginated notification inbox, newest first, including unread badge count.

**Who can call:** Authenticated user (Bearer token).

**Query params:**
- `cursor` (string, optional): Keyset cursor from previous page.
- `limit` (number, optional): Items per page, default 20 (max 50).

**Every notification has the same shape** (inbox list, `notification:new` socket event and push payload): `id`, `type`, `category`, `title`, `body`, `imageUrl`, `actor` (the other user, or null), `target: { screen, params }`, `createdAt`, `readAt`. Open `target.screen` with the ids in `target.params`.

**Notification types** (case-sensitive `type` values):

| `type` | Sent when / to whom | `target.screen` | `target.params` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MATCH_NEW` | Mutual like or auto-match, to both users | `CHAT` | `matchId`, `conversationId` |
| `MATCH_EXPIRING_SOON` | ~6 h before the 48 h clock runs out, to both users | `CHAT` | `matchId`, `conversationId` |
| `MATCH_EXPIRED` | The 48 h clock ran out, to both users (inbox only, no push) | `MATCHES` | `matchId` |
| `MESSAGE_NEW` | **Push only, never in the inbox.** Text, photo or voice message to an offline user. Date and game bubbles never send it; they have their own types | `CHAT` | `conversationId` |
| `GAME_INVITE` | A game is started, to the other player | `GAME` | `gameId`, `conversationId` |
| `GAME_COMPLETED` | Both players finished, to both | `GAME` | `gameId`, `conversationId` |
| `DATE_INVITE_RECEIVED` | Date invite sent, to the invited user | `DATE_DETAIL` | `dateId`, `matchId`, `conversationId` |
| `DATE_ACCEPTED` | Invite accepted, to the proposer | `DATE_DETAIL` | `dateId`, `matchId`, `conversationId` |
| `DATE_DECLINED` | Invite declined, to the proposer | `CHAT` | `dateId`, `matchId`, `conversationId` |
| `DATE_CANCELLED` | Date cancelled, to the other user (reason in the text) | `DATE_DETAIL` | `dateId`, `matchId`, `conversationId` |
| `DATE_POSTPONE_REQUESTED` | Postpone asked, to the other user (new day/time in the text) | `DATE_DETAIL` | `dateId`, `matchId`, `conversationId` |
| `DATE_POSTPONE_ANSWERED` | Postpone accepted or declined, to the requester | `DATE_DETAIL` | `dateId`, `matchId`, `conversationId` |
| `DATE_REMINDER` | 2 h before a confirmed date, to both users | `DATE_DETAIL` | `dateId`, `matchId` |
| `DATE_RATE_REQUEST` | Date marked completed (one day after it), to both users | `RATE_DATE` | `dateId`, `matchId` |
| `VERIFICATION_PASSED` / `VERIFICATION_REJECTED` | Face verification decided (automatic or by an admin) | `VERIFICATION` | `verificationId` |
| `ACCOUNT_WARNING` | An admin warned the user (warning text in `body`) | `WARNING` | `warningId` |
| `REPORT_REVIEWED` | A report the user filed was resolved (never reveals the outcome) | `NONE` | — |
| `STORY_PARTNER_REQUESTED`, `STORY_DECLINED`, `STORY_APPROVED`, `STORY_REJECTED` | Success-story consent and moderation steps | `STORY_DETAIL` | `storyId` |
| `ANNOUNCEMENT` | Admin broadcast | `NONE` | — |

Notifications are skipped for banned or deleted recipients, when the recipient turned that category off in notification settings, or when either user blocked the other. Inbox items are kept for 90 days.

request.description:
Registers or updates the caller's device push token (strictly one device per user policy). If the token is already registered to another user, it is reassigned to the caller.

**Who can call:** Authenticated user (Bearer token).

**Body fields:**
- `token` (string, required): FCM push token string.

Run `04 Get Eligible Dates` first to fill `{{storyDatePlanId}}` (needs a `COMPLETED` date). Submits a new success story tied to a completed date plan. Story enters PENDING_PARTNER status and triggers a consent notification to the partner.

- `title`: string, required. 1-100 characters headline.
- `body`: string, required. 1-1000 characters story text.

- `imageWidth`: integer, optional. 1-20000, pixel width of the image.
- `imageHeight`: integer, optional. 1-20000, pixel height; send together with `imageWidth`.

**Image size:** stories return `imageWidth` / `imageHeight` (integer | null) so the app can lay out the card before the image loads. When `imageUrl` came from the central upload API the server takes the size from the upload record and ignores the sent values; for other URLs it stores what the client sends; otherwise both are null. Changing `imageUrl` on edit recomputes the size.

request.description:
Updates an authored story. **Crucial rule:** Any edit invalidates previous approvals and resets status back to PENDING_PARTNER, re-requesting fresh partner consent.

**Body fields:**
- `title`: string, optional. 1-100 characters.
- `body`: string, optional. 1-1000 characters.
- `imageUrl`: string, optional. Storage URL.
- `imageWidth`: integer, optional. 1-20000, pixel width of the image.
- `imageHeight`: integer, optional. 1-20000, pixel height; send together with `imageWidth`.

**Image size:** stories return `imageWidth` / `imageHeight` (integer | null) so the app can lay out the card before the image loads. When `imageUrl` came from the central upload API the server takes the size from the upload record and ignores the sent values; for other URLs it stores what the client sends; otherwise both are null. Changing `imageUrl` on edit recomputes the size.

**Who can call it:** Super admin or admin with DISCOVERY write access.

**Body fields:**
- `values` (object, required): partial `DiscoverySettingsConfig` — sections `master`, `candidates`, `weights`, `learnedTaste`, `reRank`, `feed`, `deckRuns`, `premium` (see `01 Get Discovery Settings` for every key and default).
- `note` (string, optional): reason for the change.

**`deckRuns` section (B1 — limits for `POST /discovery/runs`):**
- `rateLimitEnabled` (boolean): hourly limit on/off. Default `true`; switch off on staging for testing.
- `maxRunsPerHour` (integer ≥ 1): new deck runs per user per hour; only in-progress runs and runs that found cards count. Default `20`.
- `deckFreshnessHours` (integer ≥ 1): how long a completed deck (even an empty one) is reused. Default `24`.
- `duplicateTapWindowSeconds` (integer ≥ 0, 0 = off): a run created this recently is returned instead of a new one. Default `5`.

Older saved versions without `deckRuns` read back with these defaults.

Invalid `deckRuns` values → `400 INVALID_DISCOVERY_SETTINGS`.

**`feed.rebuildAllPerMinute`** (integer, 1–10000, default `60`): how many users per minute **09 Rebuild All Feeds** queues. Outside the range → `400 INVALID_DISCOVERY_SETTINGS`.

**`metrics`** (D-237): `maxRangeDays` (integer 1–365, default `90`): longest period the metrics pages accept; `cacheMinutes` (integer 0–60, default `5`, `0` = no cache): how long metrics results are cached. Both apply to the Discovery **and** Auto-Matching metrics. Out of range → `400 INVALID_DISCOVERY_SETTINGS`.

request.description:
Real Discovery numbers for a period (DF-14, D-237), from swipes, matches, chat messages, date clocks and feed-build runs. Show them on the Discovery page; compare settings versions with `version`.

**Auth:** admin session cookie, module `DISCOVERY` with `READ` or `READ_WRITE`.

**Query params:** `from`, `to` (ISO 8601, default the last 30 days, longest `metrics.maxRangeDays` = 90 by default), `version` (`D{n}`, optional). Not a list, so no pagination, search or sort.

**Response `data`:** `algorithmVersion` (the `version` filter, or `null` = all versions), `currentVersion` (active settings version, e.g. `D4`), `period` (`from`, `to`, ISO 8601), `isSampleData` (now always `false`), `note` (string or `null`: a data limit worth showing), `generatedAt`, `metrics` (below). Percentages are 0–100 with one decimal; `0` when there is nothing to divide by.

**Caching:** results are cached for `metrics.cacheMinutes` (Discovery settings, default 5, `0` = off), so a number can be up to that old (`generatedAt` says when it was computed).

**Errors:** `400 INVALID_METRICS_RANGE` (bad date, or `from` after `to`); `400 METRICS_RANGE_TOO_LONG`; `400 INVALID_ALGORITHM_VERSION` (not `D` + number); `401` without a session.

**`metrics`:**
- `totalFeedBuilds`, `failedFeedBuilds`: timeline/deck builds started in the period (feed-build runs are kept 30 days, so for older periods `note` says from when they count).
- `feedBuildsPerHour`: `totalFeedBuilds` ÷ hours in the period.
- `averageBuildTimeMs`: average time from start to finish of completed builds (includes queue time).
- `buildSuccessRate`: completed ÷ (completed + failed) × 100.
- `swipesTotal`, `likesTotal`: swipes / likes (incl. super likes) made in the period.
- `likeRatePercent`: likes ÷ swipes × 100.
- `matchesTotal`: Discover matches (`source: DISCOVERY`) made in the period.
- `mutualMatchRatePercent`: matches ÷ likes × 100 (share of likes that became a match).
- `matchToConversationPercent`: share of those matches where someone wrote a message.
- `matchToDatePercent`: share of those matches where a date was accepted (the 48 h clock stopped).

request.description:
Queues a timeline feed rebuild for one user on the `discovery` BullMQ queue (job `feed_build`, job id `feed-rebuild-{userId}`, so a rebuild already waiting for that user is not doubled). Returns `202` right away; the build runs in the background and records a `discovery_runs` row (`runType: DECK`, `trigger: REFRESH`).

**Auth:** admin session cookie, module `DISCOVERY` with `READ_WRITE`.

**Path:** `{{targetNickname}}` = the user reference (`userRef`): the user's nickname (case-insensitive) or internal user id (admins only). Unknown → `404 USER_NOT_FOUND`.

**Side effects:** audit log `DISCOVERY_FEED_REBUILD_QUEUED` (category `DISCOVERY`, target = the user).

**Errors:** `404 USER_NOT_FOUND`; `409 FEED_REBUILD_NOT_ELIGIBLE` when the user has no feed (account not `ACTIVE`, onboarding not `COMPLETED`, or no location); `401` without a session.

request.description:
Queues a feed rebuild for **every eligible user** (account `ACTIVE`, onboarding `COMPLETED`, location set), spread over time at `feed.rebuildAllPerMinute` users per minute (Discovery settings, default `60`, range 1–10000). Returns `202` once everything is queued, with a `rebuildId` to follow the progress.

**One rebuild at a time (D-236):** pressing it again while a rebuild is running does not start another; it returns the running one with `reused: true` (message "A feed rebuild is already running. request.description:
Server-Sent Events stream with live progress of one "Rebuild all feeds" run (D-81 pattern, D-236). Send the admin session cookie (`EventSource` with `withCredentials: true`).

**Auth:** admin session cookie, module `DISCOVERY` with `READ` or `READ_WRITE`.

**Path:** `rebuildId` (UUID) from **09** (`{{rebuildId}}`).

**Events (named, `event:` line; case-sensitive):**
- `snapshot`: always first, the current progress object.
- `progress`: after each finished feed (built, skipped or failed).
- `completed`: once every queued user is processed (`status: COMPLETED`, `progressPercent: 100`); the stream then closes. Opening the stream for a finished rebuild sends `snapshot` + `completed` and closes.
- `ping`: every 15 s keep-alive, `data: { time }`. Ignore it.

Every `data` (except `ping`) is the progress object. **Progress object:** `rebuildId` (UUID), `status` (`QUEUEING` = users still being queued, `RUNNING`, `COMPLETED`; case-sensitive), `total` (users queued), `built` (feeds rebuilt), `skipped` (user had no feed any more or a build was already running), `failed` (build failed after its last retry), `processed` (`built + skipped + failed`), `progressPercent` (0–100; 100 only when `COMPLETED`), `perMinute`, `estimatedMinutes`, `startedAt`, `completedAt` (ISO 8601 or `null`).

**Pace:** users are spread at `perMinute`, so with 71 users at 60/min the first 60 finish in seconds and the last 11 about a minute later.

Progress is kept in Redis for **7 days**; after that the id returns `404 REBUILD_NOT_FOUND`.

**Errors (JSON, before the stream opens):** `404 REBUILD_NOT_FOUND`; `401` without a session.

request.description:
Real Auto-Matching numbers for a period (DF-14, D-237), compared with Discover matches.

**Auth:** admin session cookie, module `AUTO_MATCHING` with `READ` or `READ_WRITE`.

**Query params:** `from`, `to` (ISO 8601, default the last 30 days, longest `metrics.maxRangeDays` = 90 by default), `version` (`A{n}`, optional). Not a list, so no pagination, search or sort.

**Response `data`:** `algorithmVersion` (the `version` filter, or `null` = all versions), `currentVersion` (active settings version, e.g. `A4`), `period` (`from`, `to`, ISO 8601), `isSampleData` (now always `false`), `note` (string or `null`: a data limit worth showing), `generatedAt`, `metrics` (below). Percentages are 0–100 with one decimal; `0` when there is nothing to divide by.

**Caching:** results are cached for `metrics.cacheMinutes` (Discovery settings, default 5, `0` = off), so a number can be up to that old (`generatedAt` says when it was computed).

**Errors:** `400 INVALID_METRICS_RANGE` (bad date, or `from` after `to`); `400 METRICS_RANGE_TOO_LONG`; `400 INVALID_ALGORITHM_VERSION` (not `A` + number); `401` without a session.

**`metrics`:**
- `newcomersTotal`: users who finished onboarding in the period.
- `newcomersMatchedPercent`: share of them with at least one auto-match.
- `autoMatchesTotal`: auto-matches (`source: AUTO_MATCH`) made in the period.
- `averageMatchesCreated`: `autoMatchesTotal` ÷ `newcomersTotal`.
- `autoMatchToConversationPercent` / `autoMatchToDatePercent`: share of auto-matches where someone wrote a message / a date was accepted.
- `discoverMatchToConversationPercent` / `discoverMatchToDatePercent`: the same for Discover matches in the period (all versions), for comparison.
- `retryingCount`: users whose auto-matching is waiting for a retry **right now** (not filtered by period or version).

request.description:
Super-admin only. Retrieves current admin-tunable settings for Python Face Verification Microservice (DF-03, D-194, D-205, D-209-211).

**Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/admin/settings/verification`

**Response attributes:**
- `mode` (string): Operating mode: `AI` (automated ONNX/YuNet/SFace verification), `HOLD` (auto-pass all), or `MANUAL` (route all to admin review).
- `matchPassThreshold` (number): Face match confidence threshold for auto-pass (default: 0.40).
- `matchReviewThreshold` (number): Lower bound threshold before outright reject (default: 0.25).
- `livenessThreshold` (number): MiniFASNet anti-spoofing liveness passing threshold (default: 0.70).
- `requireGesture` (boolean): Whether V-pose peace sign is required (default: true).
- `maxAttemptsPerDay` (integer): Maximum verification attempts per 24 hours (default: 5).
- `failsBeforeReview` (integer): Consecutive failures before routing to admin review queue (default: 3).
- `cooldownSeconds` (integer): Cooldown wait time in seconds between attempts (default: 60; 0 for none).
- `selfieRetentionDays` (integer): Days before verification selfie is auto-purged from storage (default: 30).

**Verification links (B2 — verify on another device):**
- `linkEnabled` (boolean): feature on/off. Default `true`.
- `linkLifetimeMinutes` (integer 1–1440): how long a link stays valid. Default `15`. Also the window after which a selfie stuck in `QUEUED`/`PROCESSING` stops blocking new attempts.
- `linkMaxPerDay` (integer 1–100): links a user can create per 24 h. Default `10`.
- `linkBaseUrl` (URL with protocol, max 500): web page that opens links — link url = `{linkBaseUrl}/{token}`. Falls back to the `VERIFICATION_LINK_BASE_URL` env value; `null` when neither is set.
- `maxComparePhotos`: integer, max profile photos sent to vision pipeline (1..10, default 6).

Super-admin only. Updates admin-tunable settings for Python Face Verification Microservice (DF-03, D-194, D-205, D-209-211). Takes effect immediately across all backend nodes and verification workers.

**Endpoint:** `PUT /api/v1/admin/settings/verification` or `PATCH /api/v1/admin/settings/verification`

**Body fields:**
- `mode` (string, optional): One of `AI`, `HOLD`, `MANUAL` (case-sensitive).
- `matchPassThreshold` (number, optional): Face match passing threshold (0.00 - 1.00, default: 0.40).
- `matchReviewThreshold` (number, optional): Lower bound threshold before outright reject (0.00 - 1.00, default: 0.25).
- `livenessThreshold` (number, optional): Anti-spoofing liveness threshold (0.00 - 1.00, default: 0.70).
- `requireGesture` (boolean, optional): Whether V-pose gesture is required (true | false).
- `maxAttemptsPerDay` (integer, optional): Daily attempt cap per user (min: 1, max: 20, default: 5).
- `failsBeforeReview` (integer, optional): Consecutive failures before routing to admin review (min: 1, max: 10, default: 3).
- `cooldownSeconds` (integer, optional): Wait time in seconds between attempts (min: 0, max: 300; 0 for no cooldown).
- `selfieRetentionDays` (integer, optional): Days before selfie file is purged from storage (min: 1, max: 365, default: 30).
- `linkEnabled` (boolean): allow the web verification link.
- `linkLifetimeMinutes` (integer, 1–1440): how long a link stays valid.
- `linkMaxPerDay` (integer, 1–100): links a user may create per day.
- `linkBaseUrl` (URL, max 500): base URL of the verification web page.
- `maxComparePhotos` (integer, 1–20): profile photos the selfie is compared against.

**Verification links (B2 — verify on another device):**
- `linkEnabled` (boolean): feature on/off. Default `true`.
- `linkLifetimeMinutes` (integer 1–1440): how long a link stays valid. Default `15`. Also the window after which a selfie stuck in `QUEUED`/`PROCESSING` stops blocking new attempts.
- `linkMaxPerDay` (integer 1–100): links a user can create per 24 h. Default `10`.
- `linkBaseUrl` (URL with protocol, max 500): web page that opens links — link url = `{linkBaseUrl}/{token}`. Falls back to the `VERIFICATION_LINK_BASE_URL` env value; `null` when neither is set.
- `maxComparePhotos`: integer, optional (1..10). Max profile photos sent to vision pipeline.

**Also available as:** `PATCH /admin/settings/verification` (same handler, partial updates allowed the same way).

request.description:
Super-admin only. Returns the match clock (D-86, D-95, D-229): how long a new match lives without an accepted date, and when the "expiring soon" push and badge start. Both were hard-coded (48 h / 6 h) before D-229.

**Response `data`:**
- `expiryHours` (integer): hours a new match lives without an accepted date. Default 48.
- `expiringSoonHours` (integer): hours before expiry when the `MATCH_EXPIRING_SOON` push is sent and the match shows `EXPIRING_SOON`. Default 6.
- `defaults` (object): the code defaults `{ expiryHours: 48, expiringSoonHours: 6 }`.

request.description:
**Supported Methods:** Supports both `PUT` and `PATCH`.

Super-admin only. Updates the match clock (D-229). Audit-logged with the values before and after (`MATCH_CLOCK_SETTINGS_UPDATED`).

**When it applies:** to matches created, re-matched or restored by an unblock **after** the change, and to "expiring soon" timers scheduled after it. Running matches keep their current `expiresAt`. The "It's a Match!" push text uses the new hours ("…have 24 hours to plan a date.").

**Body fields:**
- `expiryHours` (integer, optional): hours a new match lives without an accepted date (range 1–720, default 48).
- `expiringSoonHours` (integer, optional): hours before expiry for the `MATCH_EXPIRING_SOON` push and `EXPIRING_SOON` status (range 1–168, default 6). Must be less than `expiryHours` (after merging with the saved values).

**Errors:** `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` (out of range / not an integer), `400 INVALID_MATCH_CLOCK_SETTINGS` (warning not shorter than the clock), `403 FORBIDDEN` (not super admin).

**Also available as:** `PATCH /admin/settings/match-clock` (same handler, partial updates allowed the same way).

response.name: 200 OK — Match Clock Settings Updated

request.description:
Updates photo gallery platform settings. Super admin only (SETTINGS module WRITE permission). Audit-logged.

**Headers:**
- `Cookie`: `admin_session={{adminSession}}`
- `Content-Type`: `application/json`

**Body fields:**
- `minPerUser`: integer, optional, 1..10. Default 1.
- `maxPerUser`: integer, optional, 0..50 (0 = unlimited). Must be >= minPerUser when > 0. Default 0.
- `maxPerRequest`: integer, optional, 1..50. Default 10.
- `captionMaxLength`: integer, optional, 0..500. Default 150.
- `previewLimit`: integer, optional, 1..20. Default 6.
- `galleryDefaultLimit` (integer, 1–100): default page size of `GET /users/:nickname/photos`.
- `galleryMaxLimit` (integer, 1–100): largest `limit` allowed there.

**Errors:**
- `400 BAD_REQUEST`: Validation failure or invalid setting ranges.
- `403 FORBIDDEN`: Caller is not a super admin.

**Also available as:** `PATCH /admin/settings/photos` (same handler, partial updates allowed the same way).
